title: Fata Morgana
text:
A blue-eyed phantom laughs

in the distance, leaping toward the west:

along a road I chase forever,

I catch my breath and hurry there.


Sunlight breaks drop by drop:

it goes singing and springing high

among the flowers with a dreamlike sound,

in a song of dreams.


I laugh, it is so swift and glad;

so far away my fancy weeps:

I hope that I may lie down someday,

lie down forever and dream.




"Fata Morgana"
editorial_note: The translation keeps Rossetti's mirage as a playful, unreachable phantom moving toward sleep and dream.

title: When I Am Dead, My Dearest
text:
When I am dead, my dearest,

sing no sad songs for me;

plant no roses at my head

nor shadowy cypress tree:

be the green grass above me,

wet with showers and dewdrops;

and if you will, remember,

and if you will, forget.


I shall not see the shadows,

I shall not feel the rain,

I shall not hear the nightingale

singing its pain:

and dreaming through a twilight

that does not rise or set,

happily I may remember,

and happily I may forget.




"When I am Dead, My Dearest"
editorial_note: The translation follows Rossetti's quiet permission to mourn gently, remember, or forget.

title: Remember
text:
Remember me when I have gone

far away into the Silent Land;

when you can no longer hold my hand,

nor I, half turning to go, still wish to stay.

Remember me when every day is ended,

when you no longer tell me of our planned future:

only remember me; you understand

it will be late then for prayers or comfort.

And if you must forget me for a while

and afterward remember, do not grieve:

for if the darkness and the sorrow leave

a trace of all the thoughts I had,

better by far that you forget and smile

than that you remember and be sad.




"Remember"
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's turn from a plea for memory toward a kinder freedom to forget.

title: De Profundis
text:
Why does the sky rise so distant?

Why does the earth hang far away?

A strange star trembles there,

shining dimly, steadily.


I do not care to reach the moon,

a circle of monotonous music;

repeating the same tune tirelessly,

far from me, far from my tenderness.


I never look at the scattered fire

of stars, or at the sun's burning road,

but all my heart shapes one desire,

a vain and withered feeling.


For I lie bound beneath the quivering spear;

joy and beauty dance beyond my reach,

I press my heart, I stretch my longing,

and tremblingly I clasp at hope.




"De profundis"
editorial_note: The translation keeps the speaker's distance from heaven, beauty, and hope as a bodily ache.

title: A Daughter of Eve
text:
A fool I was to fall asleep at noon,

and wake when the night is cold

beneath the comforting and frozen moon;

a fool to tear my rose in a frenzy,

a fool to glimpse my lilies only barely.


My poor garden I have not kept;

it faded when abandoned,

then I wept as I had never wept:

it was winter when dreams wrapped me round,

and it is summer now that I wake.


Speak as you like of a future spring,

of some warm and sweet tomorrow:

stripped of hopes and certainties,

with nothing to laugh for, nothing to sing,

I sit alone with Sorrow.




"A Daughter of Eve"
editorial_note: The translation follows the Spanish source's reversal of seasons while preserving the garden's remorse.
